title: Agreement of the finite coefficient and cocone tensor comparisons
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, $X$ any scheme, and $E\subseteq H\subseteq\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ finite intermediate extensions. Use the internal coefficient rings and canonical derived extension, restriction, adjunction and tensor comparison data of [def-weil-pbc-finite-derived-tensor-comparison]; in particular $\underline\Omega$ consists of continuous functions with image in one finite subfield. Identify the finite and algebraic-closure extension functors with [def-sfb-derived-extend-subfield] and [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar], respectively: both are total left derived extension along the same coefficient inclusions. Under these identifications the fixed comparison $\theta_{E,H}:T_{H,\Omega}T_{E,H}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{E,\Omega}$ is the canonical comparison of [def-sfb-derived-extend-comp-iso]. On the bounded constructible full subcategories, both its forward and inverse components are exactly the ambient arrows underlying the corresponding components of [def-sfb-constructible-extend-comp-iso]. This asserts equality of the specified comparisons, not merely existence of some natural isomorphism.

source.place: Exact-derived composition comparison and the canonical underived extension comparison; applied to the Hom-surj transitivity sentence

proof.text: Write $\varphi:E_X\to H_X$ and $\psi:H_X\to\Omega_X$ for the coefficient inclusions fixed in the statement. Unfold [def-weil-pbc-finite-derived-tensor-comparison], [def-sfb-derived-extend-subfield] and [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar]. The finite coefficient extension and the cocone extension both have the expression $L(\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi})$, and their algebraic-closure extensions both have the expression $L(\operatorname{Ext}_{\psi})$ (and $L(\operatorname{Ext}_{E_X\to\Omega_X})$ for the direct extension). Thus the identifications in the statement identify their actual object and arrow assignments; they do not introduce an arbitrary automorphism of a derived extension functor. In all three expressions the coefficient ring at the closure is the specified $\Omega_X$ with finite-subfield-valued sections.

source.place: First and last sentences, fixing the three extensions; the actual definitions are TwoColimit.lean, derivedExtendScalarsSubfield and derivedExtendScalarsToPadicAlgCl, and CondensedDerivedTensorComparison.lean, finiteCoefficientDerivedExtension and finiteCoefficientDerivedToAlgCl.

proof.text: Put $A=\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}$, $B=\operatorname{Ext}_{\psi}$, and $C=\operatorname{Ext}_{E_X\to\Omega_X}$. Let $c:L(BA)\xrightarrow{\sim}(LB)(LA)$ denote the fixed exact-derived composition comparison, and let $m:BA\xrightarrow{\sim}C$ denote the fixed underived tensor multiplication comparison $m_0:BA\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Ext}_{\psi\varphi}$ followed by the coefficient-map equality. The definition in [def-weil-pbc-finite-derived-tensor-comparison] is $\theta=L(m)\circ c^{-1}$. The construction of the canonical comparison $\delta$ of [def-sfb-derived-extend-comp-iso] takes the same exact-derived composition comparison and the derived image of its underived isomorphism $\theta_0:BA\xrightarrow{\sim}C$, where $\theta_0$ is the unit-compatible isomorphism between the two left adjoints $BA$ and $\operatorname{Ext}_{\psi\varphi}$ of $\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}\operatorname{Res}_{\psi}=\operatorname{Res}_{\psi\varphi}$, followed by the same coefficient-map equality. The tensor multiplication $m_0$, $s\otimes(f\otimes x)\mapsto sf\otimes x$, carries the composite unit $x\mapsto1\otimes(1\otimes x)$ of $BA\dashv\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}\operatorname{Res}_{\psi}$ to the unit $x\mapsto1\otimes x$ of $\operatorname{Ext}_{\psi\varphi}\dashv\operatorname{Res}_{\psi\varphi}$; so by the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] (with $R_1=R_2$ and $\delta=\mathrm{id}$) it is that unit-compatible isomorphism, and $m=\theta_0$. Hence $\delta=L(m)\circ c^{-1}$ as well. The source-library bodies agree literally ($\texttt{Mod.extendScalarsComp}$ is the unit-compatible $\texttt{leftAdjointUniq}$). Substitution of step 1 therefore gives $\theta=\delta$ as natural isomorphisms. No equality is inferred from the existential wording of the statement.

source.place: Exact-derived comparison followed by underived scalar-extension composition. Definitional expansion checked in lean/WeilConjectures/SixFunctors/ProEtale/ModuleObject/Colimit/TwoColimit.lean:135-147 and lean/Sheaf/AlgebraicGeometry/CondensedDerivedTensorComparison.lean:108-120; the two bodies are identical. The underived factor is matched by unit-compatibility uniqueness (def-sfb-derived-extend-comp-iso, construction step 3); lean/WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/ModuleObjects/ExtendScalars.lean:462-466 defines Mod.extendScalarsComp as leftAdjointUniq.

proof.text: Evaluate the equality of natural isomorphisms from step 2 at any ambient derived object $K$, and project to the forward and inverse natural transformations. This gives $\theta^{\mathrm{hom}}_K=\delta^{\mathrm{hom}}_K$ and $\theta^{\mathrm{inv}}_K=\delta^{\mathrm{inv}}_K$. Equality of the inverse components follows by projection of the same isomorphism equality, so no independent choice of an inverse is made.

source.place: Evaluation of the fixed natural isomorphism and its inverse.

proof.text: Let $i_E$ and $i_\Omega$ be the full inclusions of [def-sfb-dcons-subfield] and [def-sfb-dcons-qlbar], and write $\alpha$ for [def-sfb-constructible-extend-comp-iso]. Its statement specifies $\alpha$ as the restriction of $\delta$. For $K\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E)$ this means $i_\Omega(\alpha^{\mathrm{hom}}_K)=\delta^{\mathrm{hom}}_{i_EK}$ and $i_\Omega(\alpha^{\mathrm{inv}}_K)=\delta^{\mathrm{inv}}_{i_EK}$: a full-subcategory arrow is the ambient arrow between the same endpoints. In the source construction the forward and inverse components are the preimages of precisely these two ambient arrows; the full inclusion sends each preimage back to that arrow. Substituting step 3 gives $i_\Omega(\alpha^{\mathrm{hom}}_K)=\theta^{\mathrm{hom}}_{i_EK}$ and $i_\Omega(\alpha^{\mathrm{inv}}_K)=\theta^{\mathrm{inv}}_{i_EK}$, as required. The restricted comparison already has endpoints in the constructible categories, so this step needs no new preservation assertion.

source.place: Both sentences: the restricted comparison is lifted through the full inclusion; evaluate both its forward and inverse components.
